problem_statement: 657 OBSERVATION_GAP controls were classified individually in Phase 2E, falling short of equivalence_key match or flagged with 'uncertain meaning'. Testing 657 controls individually is wasteful. Solution: group by unique equivalence_key, test one representative per group, propagate result to all sibling controls.
equivalence_key_components: raw_module (e.g., Oscillator, VoiceFilter, Env, LFO, ModSlot, Arp, FXRack, Global)
methodology: Extract all 657 OBSERVATION_GAP rows from PHASE_2_FINAL_RECOUNT.json
For each control: derive its full equivalence_key (module+path+parameter+value_kind+conversion+presence+slot_rule)
Group all 657 by equivalence_key, producing N unique groups (likely 30-80 distinct keys)
For each unique group: select ONE representative control (preferably lowest-index slot)
Live-test representative in Serum 2.0.21 GUI (screenshot/tooltip readback)
If representative PASSES: promote all N sibling controls in group to AUTO_VERIFIED (verified_equivalence_key match proven)
If representative FAILS: mark entire group as MANUAL_REQUIRED with failure reason
If representative PARTIAL (e.g., LFO curve display limitation): mark as OBSERVATION_GAP_CONFIRMED_LIMITATION with workaround note

expected_outcome.unique_equivalence_keys: Approximately 40-60 distinct mechanisms across 657 controls (savings: ~11x reduction in testing)
expected_outcome.auto_verified_gain: Potentially 100-200 additional controls promoted from OBSERVATION_GAP to AUTO_VERIFIED (depending on test results)
expected_outcome.manual_required_identified: Controls whose Serum mechanism proved unsupported/unsafe for MCP authoring
expected_outcome.unresolved_confirmed: Controls whose equivalence_key failed to match any tested mechanism or showed irreducible uncertainty

critical_assumptions: Assumption 1: Controls sharing identical raw_module, raw_path, and raw_parameter MUST share identical write/read behavior (code inspection in Phase 0 shows this holds for mapping.py generic iterations)

Assumption 2: One live test per equivalence_key is sufficient proof (if oscA.volume works, oscB.volume MUST work identically per mapping.py code — this is proven by shared iteration loop, not assumption)
Assumption 3: Serum 2.0.21 behavior is consistent within a preset save/load cycle (assumption, but reasonable for production system closure)

test_plan.step_2_derive_equivalence_keys: For each 657: extract (section, canonical_id) -> derive full raw_module/path/parameter/etc. from spec.py + mapping.py evidence
test_plan.step_3_group_by_key: Use equivalence_key as dict key, accumulate all control IDs per key; count unique keys
test_plan.step_4_select_representatives: For each unique key, select representative (e.g., 'oscA' for 'osc_scalar_direct' family, 'env1' for 'env_scalar_direct', etc.)
test_plan.step_5_live_test: For each representative: launch Serum 2.0.21, load test preset with control set, readback via GUI tooltip/numeric field, document result
test_plan.step_6_propagate_result: For each group: if representative passed, bulk-promote all sibling controls to AUTO_VERIFIED; if failed, classify group as MANUAL_REQUIRED
test_plan.step_7_update_bridge: Rewrite 1,136-row bridge with new AUTO_VERIFIED count (133 + promoted_count) and updated terminal_states

risk_mitigation: RISK: A control's equivalence key appears to match but Serum's behavior differs per-slot. MITIGATION: Phase 0 code inspection proves mapping.py uses shared iteration for all slots; exception would require explicit per-slot special-case (rare, would be visible in code)
RISK: Equivalence key derivation has errors, wrong grouping. MITIGATION: Each equivalence_key derivation is documented and reviewable; code inspection of spec.py + mapping.py is the ground truth

RISK: Serum 2.0.21 changes behavior in non-obvious ways. MITIGATION: This is a system closure effort; if Serum's behavior shifts later, tests capture that as a data point for future updates, but closure can proceed on current evidence
